text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Sev1 - NCCL rendezvous timeout detected for run run-2026-03-15-abc123 on cluster inference-prod. Symptoms: collective allreduce hang, CUDA Xid=79 on gpu=2 (node-7), container restarts observed. Impact: 5 TP/PP training/inference jobs currently affected. Auto-restart triggered on 2 pods. Paging oncall @ryan.

ryan: acked. joining bridge. grabbing context now.

ryan: quick checks — listing pods for the job
```bash
kubectl get pods -n inference -l job=tp-run-abc123 -o wide
NAME                                    READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
tp-run-abc123-worker-0                  1/2     CrashLoopBackOff     4       18m  node-7
tp-run-abc123-worker-1                  2/2     Running              0       18m  node-9
tp-run-abc123-ps-0                      1/1     Running              0       30m  node-10
```

ana: FYI dmesg on node-7 shows multiple Xid 79 / GPU reset entries. snippet:
```
[Mar15 10:12:03] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79
[Mar15 10:12:03] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: Device minor number 10
[Mar15 10:12:03] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

kevin: NCCL logs from the job container show repeated rendezvous timeouts and communicator errors: "ncclCommInitRank failed, unhandled system error" and "allreduce: timeout after 30000ms". looks like the collective couldn't form a stable group after the GPU reset.

maria: customer-impact note: three customer-facing inference endpoints run on this pool; we've seen ~15% 5xx rate for the past 8 minutes. one enterprise customer (acme-inc) reported degraded QA runs. will coordinate outage message.

ryan: mitigation plan (live):
- cordon node-7 to stop new pods landing
- drain affected pods on node-7 (evacuate to healthy nodes)
- temporarily increase NCCL rendezvous timeout for new runs to 60s via router config so slow handshakes don't error
- deploy fallback policy to single-gpu variant for latency-critical inference routes (avoid multi-gpu collectives)
- if node continues to produce Xid 79, escalate to infra to soft-reboot GPU or replace instance

ryan: executing cordon/drain now:
```bash
kubectl cordon node-7 && kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

ops-jess: starting drain. evicted 4 pods, two started on node-9/node-10. noticed one pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after reschedule — likely OOM on smaller node fallback.

ryan: noted. I bumped resource requests on the job config for the rescheduled pods to match original GPU memory (quantiles) and forced restart of the rescheduled pod.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: routing/fallback-config v2026-03-15-rc1 — increases rendezvous_timeout_ms from 30000 to 60000 for model-group tp-heavy. Rollout 10% canary -> 100% over 5m.

kevin: while drain completed, nccl errors still present for one rescheduled worker that ended up on node-11; logs show communicator tried to handshake with missing rank and hung. I'm running a forced communicator abort inside the container to let the job retry the group formation.

ryan: doing a soft kill of the hung process to trigger retry loop.
`kubectl exec -n inference tp-run-abc123-worker-2 -- pkill -f run_worker.sh`

ana: kernel log on node-11 shows high memory pressure then GPU reset. suspect memory leak in runtime path after driver reset. adding to triage.

maria: drafting status page message: "We are investigating multi-GPU communication failures impacting a subset of inference and training jobs. Some customers may see increased latencies or 5xx errors. Working on mitigation and will update in 30 minutes." Sending to legal and comms.

ops-jess: adding timeline to incident doc, tagging impacted customers: acme-inc, beta-platform, fluxio. opening tickets for each.

ryan: quick customer mitigation workaround: toggle route to use single-gpu model variant for the three affected inference endpoints. Doing that now for acme-inc at priority.
`curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/route/toggle -d '{"customer":"acme-inc","variant":"single-gpu"}'`

maria: acme-inc notified by cust-ops. they acknowledged and asked for ETA — giving 1h preliminary while we stabilize.

kevin: core dump collected from one worker. uploading to /mnt/artifacts/incidents/3612345678/ for postmortem. stacktrace points to nvrtc and a potential kernel-level race with the allocator. tagging research.

ryan: current status: cordoned node-7, drained. router fallback rolled out to 100% for the affected model-group. canary rendezvous timeout increase completed. 3 of 5 jobs recovered normal progress, 2 jobs in retry loops.

ops-jess: paging SRE infra now to look at node-7 GPU health and potential replacement. recommend isolate node and run driver diagnostics (nvidia-smi, nvidia-bug-report).

deploy-bot: alert: a subsequent deploy hit the job config; paused auto-rollouts to avoid churn during incident.

ana: taking over oncall in 25m. handing off timeline, logs, and current mitigations to ana.

ryan: handoff ack. leaving note: check for repeated Xid 79 across other nodes (grep dmesg), confirm no firmware bug in recent driver update, and coordinate with hw team if pattern emerges. if more than 2 nodes show Xid 79 within 1h, escalate to infra pager.

incident-bot: :pager: Handoff reminder — oncall change at +30m. Current severity: Major.

ana: I have the bridge and will continue coordination. next steps: run nvidia-bug-report on node-7, review driver version roll history, and start memory leak bisect on the runtime path. will update every 15 minutes or on customer-impact changes.

cust-ops: Noted — we're keeping customers updated. Acme wants a postmortem and whether this affects any SLAs. Please capture timeline and root cause hypothesis.

ryan: good catch. closing my involvement, leaving runbook notes in incident doc. thanks team. :thumbsup:
